_about: Tank (Track TK, 2026-10-10: mixed warfare). ALEX'S (decision mixed-warfare): 'You have a huge ship parked off the coast but you need tanks to move inland to spot the aa batteries for the ship', mobile artillery follows tanks later, each mission has only a few elements, ground objectives start closer and engagement ranges are not settled; shared spotting is yes (any friendly unit's sight counts for its side). The unit sheet's tank (reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html genTank: 5.6 to 6.6 m long, a turret with a gun 2.8 to 4.2 m long) is the drawing, and its engine-deck panel the side's accent zone (decision unit-sheet-choices). EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track TK. The planes' movement system with a tank's numbers: the same envelope (data/units/_schema.json) on the surface band, steered by PIVOT (one flat point in the turn curve: the tracks turn it at any speed), a top speed of 10 m/s which is its speed ON A ROAD; off the road it is slower and in woods slower still (the GROUND RULE, data/sim/ground.json: speed factors on this top speed, the climb of a height step only where a road crosses it, no river without an intact bridge, no water). Two steps a turn like the boats (the design doc: 'fast aircraft get several, tanks fewer'): a step is 2.5 s, 25 m on a road at top speed, 50 m a turn. ONE LIGHT GUN on its turret, FIRED ONLY WHEN ORDERED (ALEX, 2026-10-14, decisions playtest-4 and tank-gun-orders: the gun is the tank's special, 'quick to fire again (about a 1 turn reload)', and it does not fire on its own; before that it fired by the engagement rules, decision fire-by-engagement-parameters): the turret turns to the target before it fires (decision tank-fire-feedback: 'It should delay the shot in the game so the timing is variable during the turn'), and covers a FORWARD ARC of 170 degrees (ALEX, decision playtest-3: 'Tanks should have like a forward 170 arc. Not shoot directly behind.'; it was all the way round, Track TK's proposal), the cone is level (a few degrees up and down), so it engages what stands on the ground ahead of it, never a plane overhead. It carries no bombs and has ONE SPECIAL, 'Turret Fire' (id tank_gun; the shot's numbers are data/sim/guns.json tank_gun, the turret's are this file's `turret`), which the card words with the reasons it cannot be set (decision playtest-3: 'no indication that it is engaged or why it won't engage'). Every number of the turret, the aimed shot's odds and damage, and the special is PROPOSED by builder ORD.
name: Tank

size_m._reason: the unit sheet's tank is 5.6 to 6.6 m long (genTank length), 6 m is the middle; it is the same 6 m the effects boards draw as the tank for scale (scripts/fx/fx_board_strike.gd). Two thirds of a light fighter's 9 m span

draught_m._reason: a tank does not float: only a sea unit needs water under it. The ground rule keeps it OUT of water (data/sim/ground.json)

actions_per_turn._reason: design doc: 'give each unit type a number of decision points within it, so fast aircraft get several, tanks fewer'. Two a turn like the boats (2.5 s steps): a step is 25 m on a road at top speed, short enough that the ground rule samples it every few metres and the arc is the tank's own pivot turn, and few enough that planning a tank is not tedious

health._reason: armour: tougher than a patrol boat (5) and a heavy fighter (5), well under the bomber (8). The bombs (data/sim/bombs.json) take 3 for a hit within 12 m, 2 within 25 m, 1 within 45 m, so a tank dies to two direct hits or a good stick; its own light gun does 1 pip, so a tank takes six hits from another tank's gun

sight_range_m._reason: a tank commander's view from the turret (periscopes and the hatch): a little under the battery's 700 m and the fighters' 800, and well past its own gun's 350 m, so a tank SPOTS further than it shoots - which is the job Alex gave it, to spot the anti-aircraft batteries for the ship. Line of sight (data/view/fog.json vision.eye_height_m, ground 2.5 m) cuts it where a ridge or a cliff hides the ground

material._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (2026-10-12; the board's table, variants/gunfire/board.json material_table, which Alex's decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', and gunfire-looks, G3, put to use): armour plate. Decides what a round that lands on it does (data/fx/fx.json gunfire): metal.

source_m._reason: the engine deck: about half the 6 m hull (Alex, decision impact-by-round-and-target: a small source, about 8 m at most, never the unit's length). Puffs of 1 to 2.4 m radius, at the last pip about the tank's own width

source_back_m._reason: the engine deck at the rear third of the hull: 2 m behind the centre of a 6 m tank

rise_mps._reason: the smoulder's rate: a damaged ground or sea unit smokes like a ruin or a wreck (data/fx/fx.json ruin R1 and crash A smolder rise_mps 4.0), so its puffs climb into the faster air above and the plume leans downwind (decisions smoke-consistency, wind-with-height). PROPOSED

shape._about: Alex (decision line-of-fire): 'yes, two layers, hull and turret'. A tank behind a wall or sandbags shows its turret and little hull. Heights: the lead's brief from Alex's decision, hull to about 1.5 m and turret to 2.3 m; the sizes are the unit sheet's tank (scripts/ui/unit_marker_art.gd gen_tank: length 5.6-6.6, width 2.9-3.3, hull_h 1.5-1.8, turret_h 0.75-0.95, turret_r 1.0-1.2, turret 0.2-0.55 m ahead of the middle). Every number PROPOSED.

stamp._reason: a target, not scenery: other lines are not blocked by it

length_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 6.0 m, the unit's size_m (the sheet's 5.6-6.6 m)

width_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 3.1 m, the middle of the sheet's 2.9-3.3 m

bottom_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): on the ground (the tracks are the hull's underside)

top_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 1.5 m, 'hull to about 1.5 m' (the lead's brief from Alex's decision; the sheet's hull is 1.5-1.8)

stamp._reason: a target, not scenery: other lines are not blocked by it

forward_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 0.4 m ahead of the hull's middle, where the gun's hardpoint is (the sheet: turret_y -0.55 to -0.2)

length_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 2.2 m, the sheet's round turret (turret_r 1.0-1.2)

width_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 2.2 m, as long as it is wide (a round turret)

bottom_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): on top of the hull

top_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 2.3 m, 'turret to 2.3 m' and the gun's hardpoint height (data/units/tank.json weapons)

speed_min_mps._reason: slow reverse: a tank can reverse once stopped (design doc, Motion and inertia, 'ships can reverse once stopped', and the schema's reverse_from_stop for ships and tanks)

speed_cruise_mps._reason: a steady road march, a fifth below top speed (the AI drives at it and a new tank starts at it unless a scenario says otherwise). 8 m/s is about 29 km/h

speed_max_mps._reason: about 36 km/h: a WWII tank's road speed, and the speed ON A ROAD (the lead's brief for this track, not Alex's: about 10 m/s on a road, slower off it). Off the road the ground rule cuts it (data/sim/ground.json speed_factor)

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: a tank cannot dive: equal to speed_max_mps

accel_mps2._reason: from a stop to top speed in 5 s, one turn: a heavy hull with a big engine

decel_mps2._reason: brakes and the tracks' drag: from top speed to a stop in 2.5 s, one step, which is also what lets the ground rule slow it into woods or onto a shore within a step

reverse_from_stop._reason: design doc, Motion and inertia: ships and tanks reverse only once stopped; speed cannot cross zero within a step

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: pivot steering (data/units/_schema.json: 'Tanks: one flat point'): the tracks turn it at the same rate at any speed, 30 deg/s, so a step turns it up to 75 degrees and a full circle takes 12 s (about two and a half turns). At top speed that is a turn radius of 19 m, three hull lengths

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: a tank loses a little speed in a hard turn (the track on the inside brakes): at the full rate 0.8 m/s per second, 2 m/s over a step

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: as the planes' and boats': gentle turns are nearly free, hard turns bite

altitude_bands._reason: it rides the ground: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json). Bombs reach it (they hurt a unit at the surface)

round._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (decision round-model, 2026-10-12): the tank's light gun fires a medium cannon round (the board's mapping, variants/gunfire/families.json rounds turret_gun: medium). Its muzzle smoke and its hit and miss impacts are decision gunfire-looks (G3), sized by that round's calibre

hardpoints._reason: the turret's centre as the unit sheet draws it (turret_y -0.55 to -0.2 m, i.e. 0.4 m ahead of the hull's middle) and its height (hull 1.5 to 1.8 m plus half the turret's 0.75 to 0.95 m): about 2.3 m up. The same height the fog's eye is (data/view/fog.json eye_height_m, ground 2.5 m)

mount_deg._reason: the hull's front: the arc is centred on the nose (half_across_deg 85), so a tank fires on what is ahead of it and has to turn to face a target. Was 0 with an all-round cone, where the mount did not matter

half_across_deg._reason: ALEX (decision playtest-3, the third playtest, 2026-10-11): 'Tanks should have like a forward 170 arc. Not shoot directly behind.' So the light gun covers a FORWARD arc of 170 degrees: 85 either side of the hull's nose (mount_deg 0), the full width being 2 x 85 = 170. A target behind the tank, or beside it past 85 degrees, is out of the arc and is not fired on: the tank has to turn to bring it round (its pivot turn is 30 deg/s, so a step of 2.5 s turns it up to 75 degrees and a target dead astern takes two steps). The 'about' in Alex's 'like a forward 170' is taken as exactly 170 (PROPOSED reading; the number is data). Was 180, the turret traversing all the way round (PROPOSED by Track TK, never Alex's)

elevation_deg._reason: a level cone: a light gun on a tank engages what stands on the ground, centred on the horizon

half_height_deg._reason: ten degrees up and down of the level: the target's centre is on the ground (height 0) and the gun is 2.3 m up, so a target is in the cone from 13 m out (2.3 m / tan 10 deg), which is nearer than two hulls and a gun apart; and a hill's slope fits. Not enough for a plane: even a plane in the low band (120 m) is 19 degrees up at 350 m, so a tank never shoots at one (its reach is 420 m with the overshoot, where the low band is 16 degrees up). A tank cannot answer an air attack. (Was 6 in the first draft, which left a dead zone of 22 m round the hull.)

effective_range_m._reason: short and not settled (Alex: 'I am not sure what engagement ranges make sense yet'): well inside its own sight (600 m) and the battery's flak range, so a tank spots further than it shoots. A fighter's guns reach 450 m, a heavy cannon 600 m

base_hit_chance._reason: PROPOSED by builder ORD (2026-10-14): ONE AIMED SHELL per order, not a roll a second, so the chance is a shell's: 0.6 at the cone's centre before the range and crossing factors (a target crossing at 12 deg/s halves it; a still one in range keeps it). WAS 0.12 a roll with 5 rolls a turn on its own (0.6 hits a turn at best), the rate an order every second turn (data/sim/guns.json tank_gun) cannot keep; the damage rose with it (damage_pips 2). Old note: a light gun: 0.12 a roll, a tank on a target in range makes 0.12 hits a second before the other factors, 0.6 pips a turn; the odds are the engagement parameters' (decision fire-by-engagement-parameters), the balance is not calibrated (decision balance-uncalibrated)

rim_odds_factor._reason: flat: a turret gun is aimed by its gunner anywhere in the arc, like every turret and flexible gun

falloff_exponent._reason: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: a powered turret tracks slower than a flexible machine gun (20 to 60) and a bomber's turrets (30): 12 deg/s. A target crossing at 10 m/s at 150 m is 3.8 deg/s, so it costs almost nothing, at 30 m it is 19 deg/s and the odds fall to a third

damage_pips._reason: PROPOSED by builder ORD (2026-10-14): a cannon shell, two pips (a machine gun's round is one). With one aimed shell every second turn at 0.6 the tank does about as many pips a turn as the 1-pip gun that rolled every second (about 0.5 against about 0.4): three hits kill a tank of 6 pips. WAS 1

rolls_per_second._reason: NOT USED since the gun is an order-only weapon (fires_on_special): an order makes shots_per_order aimed rolls (data/sim/guns.json). Kept because the unit schema asks for it; was one aimed shell a second

traverse_dps._reason: PROPOSED by builder ORD (2026-10-14; Alex, decision tank-fire-feedback: the turn delays the shot): a powered tank turret turns about 25 degrees a second (the lead's example), so a swing of 85 degrees takes 3.4 s and the whole 170 degrees of the arc 6.8 s, longer than a 5 s turn. A target dead ahead is on bearing at once; the hull's own pivot (30 deg/s) helps bring the arc round

half_arc_deg._reason: the weapon's forward arc (ALEX, playtest-3: 'Tanks should have like a forward 170 arc. Not shoot directly behind.'): 85 either side of the nose. The turret cannot turn past it; a target outside it is out of the arc and the hull has to come round

barrel_tip_m._reason: the drawn gun's tip from the turret's axis (the weapon's hardpoint): 5.2 m from the hull's centre less the turret's 0.4 m (data/fx/fx.json gunfire.muzzle.weapons.turret_gun tip_m, measured 2026-10-12 on the sheet's tank). Where the muzzle smoke starts, along the turret's bearing
